candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether Instacart’s ad tools increasingly influence SKU ranking and product discovery rather than merely adding ad load to an existing grocery marketplace.

candidates.sector_or_industry: Grocery marketplace, retail media, ecommerce enablement
candidates.theme_relation: If grocery discovery and replenishment are increasingly mediated by search, browse, sponsored products and AI-assisted shopping, Instacart is a reference platform showing how retail media and product discovery infrastructure monetize consumer intent.

candidates.next_evidence: Check latest 10-K, customer disclosures and product pages for vertical revenue mix, ecommerce/retail customer growth, AI-search citation metrics, net retention and evidence that structured data drives measurable consumer discovery outcomes.
candidates.node_relation: Machine-readable brand and location data layer: manages structured facts, listings, reviews, search and analytics that may influence how AI and traditional search systems surface brand/product/location answers.

candidates.why_include: Yext positions itself around structured data, listings, reviews, search and AI/traditional discovery. This creates plausible exposure to the node, but product-content and retail-media purity appear weaker than SPSC or CRTO.
candidates.why_underfollowed: Small-cap software name with messy categorization: local listings, reputation, search, analytics and agentic marketing. That makes the AI-shopping relevance easy to miss but also easy to overstate.

memory_update.text: SPSC should be carried forward as the cleanest underfollowed retail-data/plumbing candidate for AI-mediated product discovery, especially around item data, fulfillment, inventory and supplier compliance workflows.
CRTO should be carried forward as the most direct small-cap retail-media platform candidate, but later layers must separate retail-media growth from legacy retargeting/ad-tech exposure.

YEXT should remain in the speculative shadow lane until evidence proves AI-search and structured-brand-data adoption is translating into retail/ecommerce revenue rather than generic marketing positioning.
The node appears to split into three investable sublayers: marketplace/retailer-owned demand surfaces, independent retail-media monetization platforms, and product/brand/availability data plumbing.

Many pure-play product information management, content syndication, reviews and digital shelf analytics leaders appear private or acquired, so public-market exposure may be indirect through broader commerce, ad-tech and retail supply-chain software names.

node: AI-mediated shopping, retail data and product-content infrastructure
summary: Layer 1B expands the direct public-company universe for the node where consumer discovery shifts from human browsing and brand awareness toward machine-readable product facts, availability, retail-media bidding, ratings/reviews and marketplace ranking. The strongest direct exposures found in this pass are retail-media platforms and retail product-data networks rather than consumer brands themselves. Reference/context anchor: Instacart, because it owns grocery marketplace demand, retail-media inventory and closed-loop shopper data. Underfollowed lane: SPS Commerce, Criteo and Yext. SPS Commerce is the cleanest retail data/plumbing candidate; Criteo is the most direct independent retail-media monetization candidate; Yext is a smaller, more speculative AI-discovery structured-data candidate. This is not a buy/sell list; later layers must verify revenue sensitivity to AI shopping and retail-media adoption rather than generic ecommerce or ad-tech exposure.
